target.discreteness: only 776 distinct values across 15289 train rows (most frequent value repeats 33 times) — the target has a small finite support, the fingerprint of a synthetic dataset resampled from a much smaller original table. Under an MAE metric a discrete support is exploitable post-processing, not a curiosity.
target.sample_submission_constant: 6025.194 = the train mean, so the sample submission is the mean baseline; MAE prefers the median (6117.4759), which is already a free improvement over it

test_window.evidence: no date/time column in any file; id is a single contiguous integer range split at 15289 (train 0..15288, test 15289..25482), which encodes row order not time. All 16 feature columns are static agronomic/weather-profile attributes of a simulated blueberry field plot. config.yaml description is 'Predict wild blueberry yield' with problem_type: regression — no forecasting or grouped-holdout framing anywhere in the available inputs. Train and test share the same low-cardinality feature levels (spot-checked on clonesize, the TRange block and RainingDays).

split_policy.scheme: shuffled KFold (5-fold or 10-fold), stratified on binned yield (bins over the continuous range; the discrete 776-value support means plain KFold can shift fold target distributions more than usual at this row count)
split_policy.forbidden: no time-based constraint applies (no date column); do NOT group by the low-cardinality weather profile — test shares the identical profile levels as train, so a grouped split would understate the achievable score
split_policy.rationale: TASK-TS-FUTURE does not trigger — no date column, no forecasting framing, contiguous id split. The 4.5x optimism bias that motivates the time-split mandate is not in play here.
split_policy.caveat: 14 exact duplicate feature-rows inside train and 18 test rows with an exact feature match in train — small enough to ignore for CV design, but note that duplicates spanning folds mildly inflate CV; verify magnitude in Stage 1.

metric.name: MAE
traps: L1 objective is mandatory for training (objective='mae'/'l1'/MAE loss), not L2 — TASK-MAE-METRIC. An RMSE-trained model is fitting the conditional mean while the metric scores the conditional median; on a target this skewed (median 6117 vs mean 6025) that gap is real.

the target's support is 776 discrete values — snapping/rounding predictions onto the observed train target support (or onto a coarser quantile grid) is a candidate free gain under MAE. It MUST be applied inside the metric function so every blend candidate and every tree-search node is scored on the post-processed value, never bolted on at the end.
clip predictions to the observed train target range [1945.53, 8969.40] inside the same post-processing step

blend weights for an MAE metric have NO closed form — the NNLS shortcut that applies to RMSE-family metrics (TASK-BLEND-DECOR) is invalid here. Optimize weights directly against the MAE objective (coordinate/simplex search or an L1 linear program on OOF), and score every candidate weight vector through the same post-processing.

MAE is scale-sensitive and unnormalized: absolute score magnitudes are in yield units (~300-400 for a good model), so relative deltas look tiny — compare with enough OOF precision to distinguish members.

external_data.evidence: config.yaml special_rules sets external_data_allowed: false, pretrained_models_allowed: false, internet_access_allowed: false — external data is prohibited outright, so no candidate may be proposed. Independently, no whitelist source has a derivable join key: there is no country, no date, no currency and no geographic column anywhere in the schema, so World Bank (country x year), holiday calendars (country x date), ISO tables (country), ECB rates (currency x month) and OWID COVID (country x date) are all unjoinable. The features are simulated agronomic inputs from a spatially-explicit pollination model, not observations tied to a real place or time.
external_data.note: The original Wild Blueberry Yield dataset (Aygun et al.) that this playground data was generated from is a commonly-used augmentation source for this competition family, but it is NOT on the Stage 0.5 whitelist and external_data_allowed is false — it is therefore excluded, not merely deprioritized.

data_level: collapse the six TRange columns — MaxOfUpperTRange, MinOfUpperTRange, AverageOfUpperTRange, MaxOfLowerTRange, MinOfLowerTRange, AverageOfLowerTRange are pairwise correlated at >= 0.998 and take only 5-6 distinct joint levels. They encode ONE ordinal weather-severity factor. Replace them with a single ordinal index (rank of AverageOfUpperTRange) plus, optionally, the derived spreads (Upper-Lower average gap, Max-Min range) which are the only non-redundant information in the block.
same collapse for the rain block: RainingDays and AverageRainingDays are near-duplicates (corr -0.477 and -0.484 with the target); keep one plus their ratio/product as a rain-intensity proxy

pollinator aggregate features: honeybee + bumbles + andrena + osmia total density, per-species shares of that total, and a wild-vs-managed split (bumbles+andrena+osmia vs honeybee) — the underlying model is a pollination simulation, so total and composition of pollinators are the physically meaningful quantities, not the four raw densities

fruitset, fruitmass and seeds are by far the strongest signals (corr 0.886 / 0.826 / 0.869 with yield) and are themselves near-outputs of the same simulation: build their ratios and products (seeds*fruitmass = implied mass per fruit-set unit, fruitset*seeds, fruitmass/seeds) — these compose multiplicatively into yield in the generative model

treat the 13 of 16 low-cardinality columns (nunique <= 20) as categorical for the GBDTs' native categorical handling as a distinct feature view — TASK-CAT-ONLY does not fully trigger (columns are numeric and three are continuous) but the encoding lever it points at is partially live here
honeybee is heavy-tailed (max 18.43 against a typical 0.25-0.75) — a log1p / winsorized view of it as an alternative feature representation for a decorrelated member
interaction of the collapsed weather ordinal with clonesize and with pollinator totals — the simulation couples temperature, clone size and pollination
model_level: L1 / MAE objective throughout (LightGBM objective='mae' or 'regression_l1', XGBoost 'reg:absoluteerror', CatBoost loss_function='MAE') — TASK-MAE-METRIC, this is the single highest-leverage model-level choice

post-processing INSIDE the metric function for every candidate: clip to the train target range, then evaluate snapping to the observed 776-value target support (and a coarser rounding grid) as a scored variant, not as an unvalidated finish
GBDT trio (LightGBM / XGBoost / CatBoost) as the core pool — 15k rows x 16 all-numeric low-cardinality columns is exactly their regime; expect the pool to be variance-dominated

TASK-BLEND-DECOR: add one shallow, heavily regularized, different-library bias-dominated member as a decorrelator — here a quantile/L1 regularized linear model (or a small MLP with L1 loss) over the engineered ratio features. Its solo score will look poor; that is not a reason to drop it before weight optimization.

because fruitset/fruitmass/seeds dominate, an explicitly low-feature model (those three plus the weather ordinal) is a natural high-bias blend member and a useful sanity check against overfitting the 13 weak columns
blend weight search must optimize MAE directly (not NNLS) — see metric.traps

partial_task_priors.reason: 13 of 16 feature columns have nunique <= 20 (clonesize 6, the TRange block 5-6 each, RainingDays 6, pollinators 7-16), so the encoding lever the prior points at is live — but the columns are float64 numeric with meaningful ordinal magnitude, and the three strongest features (fruitset, fruitmass, seeds) are genuinely continuous. Use it as a feature-view idea (native categorical handling as one member), not as the governing strategy.

rejected_task_priors.reason: no date column, no forecasting framing, contiguous id split with identical train/test feature-level support
no daily-resolution series and no country/store/product keys
16 columns x 15289 rows — rows greatly exceed columns, the opposite regime
single scalar target, no grid/sequence output and no explicit generative rule exposed in the data

downstream_checks_for_stage_1: verify the iid hypothesis with adversarial validation (train-vs-test AUC near 0.5 confirms; above ~0.6 refutes it and forces a re-derived split policy)
confirm the 776-value discrete target support and measure the OOF MAE delta from snapping predictions onto it — this is the dossier's main exploitable hypothesis and must be scored, not assumed
quantify the redundancy of the TRange block explicitly (rank / joint-level count of the six columns) before committing to the collapse to one ordinal
measure how much target variance fruitset/fruitmass/seeds alone explain, to size the payoff of engineering the other 13 columns at all
check whether the 14 in-train duplicate feature-rows carry conflicting targets (they would cap achievable MAE) and whether the 18 exact train-test feature matches are worth a direct lookup
not_recorded: public/private leaderboard split ratio — not stated in config.yaml and no leaderboard page was consulted
official competition rules text — only config.yaml's special_rules block was available; the external-data verdict rests on that block, not on the rules page

whether the synthetic generation used the original Aygun et al. Wild Blueberry Yield table and, if so, whether the competition rules would have permitted joining it — config.yaml's external_data_allowed: false settles the action regardless, but the underlying rules text was not read
number of submissions already used against the daily limit of 5
units and physical meaning of the TRange columns (degrees F is likely from the value ranges 39-94.6, but no data dictionary was available)
